title: Server-render game archive pages with Astro instead of building cards in the browser
description:
`/games` and `/season/[season]/games` are still using Astro mostly as a shell around a client-side mini app.

Current shape:
- `website/src/components/GameListView.astro` renders empty containers, a `Loading games...` placeholder, and a `<script type="application/json" id="game-list-config">` blob containing the full game list.
- `website/src/scripts/game-list.js` is 577 lines of client-side DOM construction, filter state management, and card rendering.
- The actual game cards do not exist in the HTML sent by Astro; they only appear after JS runs.

That leaves performance and consistency on the table:
- Slower first paint / LCP on the main archive pages.
- A loading state for content that is already fully known at build time.
- More JS than necessary for a page that is mostly static markup.
- Harder testing, because correctness depends on post-load DOM mutation.

Suggested fix:
1. Render the initial game cards in Astro on the server.
2. Make filters either URL-driven server rendering or a small client island that progressively enhances already-rendered markup.
3. Keep only the minimal interactive behavior hydrated on the client.

A good outcome is that `/games` and `/season/[season]/games` still support the same filters, but the page HTML already contains the archive cards before any client JS runs.
